queue.name: Iran-Iraq Gas Pipeline (Basra / Shalamcheh line)
queue.note: Two physical Iranian export lines into Iraq (Naft Shahr->Baghdad/Diyala, 2013 contract; Shalamcheh->Basra, 2015 contract, flows from mid-2018) but only one generic roster row, P5855 (cap 35.00) — whichever line P5855 does not represent is missing; vetting must first pin down which border crossing P5855 covers.

evidence.note: NIGC and Iraq's Ministry of Electricity signed a SECOND gas export contract (Nov 2015) specifically for Basra: 7 mcm/d initially, ramping to 20-35 mcm/d (35 mcm/d peak in the five hot months), for power generation — separate from the 2013 Baghdad contract.
Iran exporting 32 mcm/d to Iraq; commitments cover both Baghdad (plus Diyala) AND Basra — two distinct delivery obligations/lines; first Basra flows dated to mid-2018 by EIA and trade press.

queue.name: Kurdistan-Turkey Gas Export Pipeline
queue.note: Roster carries only domestic KRI segments (P4047 Khormor-Erbil, P4053 Erbil-Duhok, P7457 Semel-Duhok), all terminating inside Iraq; the cross-border Duhok->Fishkhabour->Turkey export leg (2013 KRG-Turkey framework, 2017 Rosneft 30 bcm/y BOOT deal) is uncaptured — vetting should also check GEM's Turkey roster and whether GEM treats P4053 as the first leg of this scheme.

evidence.note: KRG MNR: under the Nov 2013 KRG-Turkey agreements, KRG to export >10 bcm/y via a dedicated export pipeline with a new KRG metering station north of the federal Fishkhabour station; export line described as distinct from the domestic Khor Mor-Erbil network.

2021 KAR Group contract to expand the network from PUK-area fields to Erbil and onward to Dohuk near the Turkish border, with the ultimate goal of connecting to Turkish infrastructure for export; stalled by KDP-PUK dispute but export ambition still live.

New 52-inch line extending toward the Turkish border built 'with extra capacity for more destinations in the future, including potential exports' — domestic Erbil-Duhok segment sized for a future cross-border export leg.

Rosneft press release (18 Sep 2017): agreement to fund and build a gas pipeline in Iraqi Kurdistan handling up to 30 bcm/yr for export plus domestic supply; BOOT structure; domestic supply from 2019, exports from 2020.
Rosneft agreed to construct a 30 bcm/yr gas pipeline to Turkey; project stayed in development phase, never reached construction; Rosneft later partially divested.

queue.name: Iraq-Jordan Gas Pipeline (Basra-Aqaba gas leg)
queue.note: No Jordan-touching gas line in the roster; the gas leg of the 2013 Basra-Aqaba twin pipeline (dropped in the 2017 oil-only downscoping, briefly revived 2018) is distinct from P7573 Basra-Ceyhan and from the oil-tracker Basra-Aqaba line, and GEM does track cancelled cross-border proposals (cf. P0450, P0481).

evidence.note: April 2013 Iraq-Jordan agreement for an $18bn twin pipeline Basra->Aqaba: 1 million bpd crude PLUS a parallel natural gas line to supply Jordan (~258 MMcf/d on the Jordanian stretch).
Jordan approved construction of the new oil AND gas double pipeline from Basra to Aqaba.
Iraqi cabinet re-approved the Basra-Aqaba project as a twin oil and gas pipeline — brief revival of the gas leg before the project was again downscoped to oil-only.

queue.name: Akkas-Syria Gas Pipeline
queue.note: No Iraq-Syria gas line in the roster: P0450 (Iran-Iraq-Syria Friendship line, cancelled) carries Iranian gas and P1841 Baiji-K3-Al Kaem terminates at Al-Qa'im inside Iraq; the Akkas->Arab Gas Pipeline export link is a separate never-captured cross-border proposal, newly relevant with SLB restarting Akkas drilling (Jan 2026) and post-Assad AGP revival talk.

evidence.note: Akkas Gas Pipeline (aka Iraq-Europe Gas Pipeline), planned as early as 2009, from Akkas in al-Anbar through Syria to the Arab Gas Pipeline toward Turkey/Europe; stalled by the Syrian war and ISIS's 2014 seizure of Akkas; listed among corridors under renewed post-Assad discussion; SLB began drilling at Akkas Jan 2026.

In September 2004 Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Lebanon agreed to connect the Arab Gas Pipeline with Iraq's gas grid to allow Iraqi gas exports toward Europe — long-standing framework for an Iraq-Syria gas interconnection.

queue.name: Halfaya-Kahla Gas Pipeline
aka: Halfaya GPP-Amara/Maysan power plants gas supply line
queue.note: No roster row covers gas leaving Halfaya (P6832 is the INBOUND Buzurgan->Halfaya sour-gas leg; P4058 Eastern Iraq at 48in does not match the 24in/21km spec) — this dry-gas outlet has operated since 2013 and now carries Halfaya GPP output to the Amara/Maysan power stations; vetting should check P4058's route to rule out corridor overlap.

evidence.note: 24-inch, ~21 km pipeline from Halfaya field to a gas collection unit near the Al-Kahla power station; pilot deliveries of 40 MMcf/d to the 180 MW plant — first operational associated-gas project of Iraq's second bid round.
300 MMscf/d Halfaya associated-gas processing facility opened; dry gas delivered to the Amara and Maysan power plants, feeding >1,200 MW of generation in Maysan governorate.

queue.name: Chemchemal-Bazian Gas Pipeline
aka: Chemchemal field dedicated industrial gas pipeline
queue.note: No roster entry originates at the Chemchemal field — this is a newly announced (Jan 2026 GSAs), privately funded, dedicated 40 km line from Chemchemal to Bazian industrial consumers (cement/steel, up to 142 MMscf/d, deliveries H2 2027), distinct from Khor Mor-sourced P6823 (feeds Bazian POWER plants) and P4047.

evidence.note: Official Crescent Petroleum press release: GSAs for up to 142 MMscf/d from Chemchemal for 10 years starting H2 2027; 'a dedicated 40-kilometer pipeline linking the Chemchemal field directly to industrial consumers in the Bazian area' to be built by private-sector companies; $160m committed.
Independent trade-press coverage confirming the 142 MMscf/d offtake, H2 2027 start, and new private-sector pipelines to Bazian and Erbil.
Analysis confirming Chemchemal development (Dana Gas/Crescent/Pearl consortium) with 'a dedicated 40-kilometre pipeline' connecting Chemchemal to the Bazian industrial area, deliveries from H2 2027.
Independent report of the same KRG-sanctioned offtake deals: Chemchemal gas to flow in 2027 with new dedicated pipeline infrastructure to Bazian.
Operator's own site confirms the Chemchemal development program under the KRG-granted concession (drilling, well testing, infrastructure construction; ~$160m program).

queue.name: Chemchemal-Erbil industrial gas supply pipeline
queue.note: Announced only as 'new pipelines... to supply gas to industrial users in Erbil' (offtaker Van Steel) alongside the Bazian line — no roster entry covers a Chemchemal-to-Erbil industrial supply line, but vetting must decide whether this is a standalone build or a tie-in delivering via the existing/under-construction Khor Mor-Erbil corridor (P4047).

evidence.note: Press release states 'new pipelines are to be built by private-sector companies to supply gas to industrial users in Erbil and Bazian' — a second build serving the Erbil offtaker (Van Steel) in addition to the dedicated 40 km Bazian line; no route/length given.
Corroborates that new private-sector pipelines will supply industrial users in both Erbil and Bazian ahead of H2 2027 first gas.

queue.name: Miran gas field export pipeline (to Bazian power plant)
queue.note: Early-stage lead with a firm field-development contract (May 2025 HKN+ONEX JV, first gas targeted 2H 2027) but the ~30-40 km evacuation pipeline to the Bazian power plant is only implied (MEES names Bazian PP as destination); no Miran-related pipeline exists anywhere in the roster — vetting applies the add-threshold, specs not yet public.

evidence.note: MEES (paywalled beyond headline/standfirst): Miran partners fast-tracking a 100 MMcf/d gas processing plant with first gas 2H 2027; the gas to feed the nearby Bazian power plant — implying a new evacuation pipeline from Miran.
19 May 2025 Washington signing: HKN Energy + ONEX form Miran Energy JV with KRG to develop the ~8 tcf Miran field in phases, initial focus on domestic supply; pipeline not yet specified.

queue.name: Diyala Gas Fields Supply Pipeline (Gilabat-Qumar / Khashim Ahmer-Injana to Diyala power plants)
aka: Crescent Petroleum Diyala gas project pipelines
queue.note: No roster row covers a new-build line from the Gilabat-Qumar / Khashim Ahmer-Injana fields to Diyala power plants (P4058 Eastern Iraq is believed to be the existing import corridor, not this build); volumes ramp ~120-250 toward ~520 MMscfd (transmission scale) — vetting should confirm it is not within the field/plant boundary.

evidence.note: Crescent press release on three 20-year contracts: Diyala fields to initially produce 250 MMscfd; 'The company will build a processing plant on site as well as pipelines and infrastructure to supply gas'; first gas expected within 18 months to supply nearby power plants.
Same press release via Zawya, independently confirming the pipelines-and-infrastructure scope for supplying Diyala power plants from Gilabat-Qumar and Khashim Ahmer-Injana.
First phase of 3D seismic at Khashim al Ahmer (Diyala) completed April 2025 — project active but still in appraisal, so the supply pipeline is most likely still pre-construction.

queue.name: Al-Faw Grand Port LNG-Abu Ghraib Supply Pipeline
aka: Abu Ghraib IPP gas supply pipeline
queue.note: No roster line runs from Al-Faw Grand Port northward into the network (not P7435 Khor Al-Zubair FSRU tie-in, not P7434, and shelved P5857 Zubair-Faw is a smaller 18in/105km line in the opposite delivery direction) — cabinet-approved Aug 2025 as 130 km of connecting pipeline toward the Abu Ghraib 3,000 MW CCGT plus a bundled 17 km FSRU-to-plant line at Al-Faw; 130 km cannot physically reach Abu Ghraib, so it is most likely the port-to-national-grid trunk segment.

evidence.note: Cabinet approvals of 26 August (per PM's media office): Al-Faw Grand Port LNG reception infrastructure includes 'a jetty, a floating storage and regasification unit, and connecting pipelines — 17 kilometres at Al-Faw and 130km at Abu Ghraib'; each plant allocated ~400 MMscf/d of imported LNG; 25-year BOO with GE Vernova technology.
Corroborates the cabinet-approved package: Abu Ghraib 3,000 MW CCGT supplied with 'imported LNG via 130 km pipeline from Al-Faw port'; Al-Faw 3,000 MW plant supplied via 17 km pipeline from the FSRU.

dropped.reason: duplicate-of-candidate: identical project (same 40 km Chemchemal field -> Bazian industrial line, same Jan 2026 GSAs) as the news strategy's Chemchemal-Bazian Gas Pipeline; evidence merged into chemchemal-bazian-gas.
